title: A Codex whose approval was answered stops needing you
notes: The fake codex used to leave an answered approval on screen, in Claude's words, so trix, which reads an untrusted Codex's prompts off its screen, kept it on needs-you for good after the answer. A real Codex takes the dialog away once answered. This checks trix's Codex path without trusted hooks: needs-you from Codex's own approval wording, and not after the answer.

args.text: Would you like to run the following command?
args.why: Codex asks in its own words
the answered dialog is gone, as in Codex

args.text: You approved codex to run rm -rf dist this time
args.why: the answer is on record instead
and it doesn't come back once the screen settles
